primary: Machine-learning researchers from other subfields (adjacent researchers): they know general ML, deep learning, standard evaluation practice, and statistics, but not this project's subfield-specific terminology, datasets, or prior work.
secondary: Reviewers/replicators checking the paper's claims against the evidence in project/paper.txt and project/README_1.md.
tertiary: Future readers and practitioners who encounter MLPerf Tiny cited elsewhere and want a self-contained account of what it is and what its first round showed.
assumed_known: quantization as a general concept (that lower-precision numerics exist)
the idea of a community benchmark suite (e.g. from mainstream ML benchmarking culture)
not_assumed: TinyML as a named field and its resource envelope
post-training quantization (PTQ) vs. quantization-aware training (QAT) terminology
closed/open submission divisions as MLPerf Tiny defines them
the specific benchmarks (CoreMark, MLMark, MLPerf Inference) and how they differ
the four component datasets/reference models (Speech Commands/DS-CNN, VWW/MobileNetV1, CIFAR-10/ResNet, DCASE2020/FC-autoencoder) and why each was chosen
